Malignant epithelial cells in these patients showed elevated expression of VEGFA and VEGFB , leading to the expansion of RGCC+ ECs, which express high levels of VEGFR2 . These ECs, along with MMP11+ CAFs formed a collagen-rich niche that actively suppressed immune infiltration and promoted immunosuppressive cell recruitment. Both RGCC+ ECs and MMP11+ CAFs exhibited robust expression of collagen-related genes such as COL4A1 , COL1A1 , and COL6A3 , suggesting a shared functional role in extracellular matrix remodeling. Furthermore, these stromal populations engaged in reciprocal activation loops via collagen-associated receptor–ligand pairs, reinforcing the structural and biochemical barriers to effective immune surveillance. ST analyses confirmed the close proximity of RGCC+ ECs, MMP11+ CAFs and TNFRSF4+ Tregs, forming a tightly integrated immunosuppressive network. Notably, RGCC+ ECs also expressed PLVAP , a marker associated with endothelial tip cells and immunomodulatory function, further supporting their role in shaping the suppressive landscape. 63 Importantly, our findings extend beyond the physical exclusion of immune cells by collagenous matrices. We demonstrate that VEGF-driven stromal reprogramming actively orchestrates immune evasion by promoting the formation of a structured immunosuppressive niche. 24 This mechanism provides a rationale for targeting both angiogenesis and collagen remodeling as complementary strategies to dismantle this barrier. Clinically, the presence of collagen-high stromal subpopulations in non-responders suggests their potential utility as predictive biomarkers and therapeutic targets. Among these, RGCC+ ECs stand out due to their high expression of VEGFR2 and their central role in vascular-immune crosstalk. Recent studies have shown that anti-VEGF therapies could enhance the efficacy of PD-1 and CTLA-4 blockade in cholangiocarcinoma. Moreover, emerging evidence indicates that blocking the VEGF–VEGFR2 signaling axis in Tregs may disrupt their suppressive function and promote antitumor immunity. 91 Clinical trials have already underscored the benefits of combining anti-angiogenic agents targeting VEGFR2 with immunotherapy or chemotherapy across various relapsed and refractory tumors. 80 92 93 Building on these observations, we confirmed the therapeutic potential of VEGFR2 inhibition in both ESCC cell lines and murine models, demonstrating that it significantly enhances the antitumor effects of PD-1 blockade and standard chemotherapeutic regimens. We recognize that a small sample size may have limited our ability to identify features correlated with response. Additionally, we acknowledge that driver mutation status, including p53 mutations, was not available for this cohort, as targeted sequencing is not part of routine clinical practice and biopsy material was limited. Future studies integrating genomic and transcriptional profiling with targeted sequencing will be essential. Such studies will help explore the relationship between cancer cell intrinsic driver mutations and key features including high CNV burden, genomic instability, mutational burden, and immunogenicity. Additionally, they will facilitate investigation into how these mutations influence TME reprogramming and treatment efficacy. Furthermore, our integrated spatial and single-cell analyses reveal a strong correlation in non-responders: the abundance of RGCC+ ECs and MMP11+ CAFs, together with the collagen-rich matrix they deposit, is associated with restricted immune infiltration. We acknowledge that these observational findings do not establish definitive causality. Definitive evidence will require in vivo loss-of-function studies, including genetic ablation of RGCC+ ECs or MMP11+ CAFs, as well as targeted disruption of the collagen barrier, to rigorously establish whether these stromal features directly drive therapeutic resistance. Our functional signature analyses highlight that neoadjuvant therapy drives profound functional reprogramming within the immune compartment, independent of macroscopic numerical changes. Importantly, the highly heterogeneous and subset-specific nature of these transcriptomic shifts underscores the extreme complexity of TME remodeling. Consequently, while transcriptomic plasticity clearly underpins therapeutic efficacy, fully disentangling the precise mechanisms of this multifaceted immune rewiring will require sophisticated functional studies in the future. Taken together, our study establishes a comprehensive single-cell atlas of the TME in patients with ESCC undergoing NACI. It identifies key cellular mediators of response—including ACKR1+ ECs, CFD+ CAFs, and RGS1+CD8+ T cells—and delineates a resistance signature dominated by RGCC+ ECs, MMP11+ CAFs, Tregs, APOE+ macrophages, and angiogenesis-active malignant cells. Critically, our spatial and functional analyses reveal how these components interact in a coordinated manner to either support or suppress antitumor immunity. These findings provide a strong foundation for developing novel combination therapies that target both immune and stromal compartments to overcome resistance and improve outcomes in ESCC. By integrating mechanistic insights with preclinical validation, our work highlights the importance of tailoring therapeutic strategies to the specific architecture of the tumor microenvironment, paving the way for more precise and effective treatments in this challenging disease setting.
